title: Mrs. Michal Tawil: My Husband did not Wait for me for Kidush (class #21)

chapters.title: Understanding hagdara and gader
chapters.about: Defining one's own identity and boundaries

chapters.title: Lessons from the Parasha
chapters.about: Moshe Rabbenu, the rock, and trusting Hashem

claims: She explains that when we hold rigid expectations of how others should behave, such as a husband waiting for his wife to make Kiddush, we become depleted and angry when reality differs from our internal picture.
Instead, she encourages listeners to recognize that all situations are orchestrated by Hashem for our personal growth and to respond with flexibility and inner strength.
summary: Mrs. Tawil discusses the importance of maintaining one's own 'gader' or fence, which represents one's personal identity and description, rather than entering the 'fence' of others. She explains that when we hold rigid expectations of how others should behave, such as a husband waiting for his wife to make Kiddush, we become depleted and angry when reality differs from our internal picture. Instead, she encourages listeners to recognize that all situations are orchestrated by Hashem for our personal growth and to respond with flexibility and inner strength.
questions: How can I stop feeling depleted when others do not meet my expectations?
What does it mean to stay within my own 'fence' or description?
How should I handle situations that are baffling or frustrating?
Is it wrong to have expectations of my spouse or family members?
How can I turn a difficult situation into an opportunity for growth?
